sections.h2: Where do you pay and question property tax in Lowndes County?
sections.html:
Lowndes County runs its property tax from Valdosta, and the commissioner and the assessors answer different kinds of questions. Bills, payments and liens belong to the commissioner. Values and special assessment programs belong to the assessors.

  • Lowndes County Tax Commissioner: 300 N. Patterson Street, P.O. Box 1409, Valdosta, GA 31601. Phone 229-671-2579, fax 229-671-2599. Open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM, with the drive-thru window open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM.
  • Lowndes County Board of Tax Assessors: phone (229) 671-2540.
  • Clerk of Superior Court deed room, Lowndes County Judicial Complex, 327 N. Ashley Street, 1st Floor, Valdosta: copies of your warranty deed.

The commissioner's office keeps a drive-up drop box in the front parking lot of the Government Building, on the right-hand side. If you mail a check, write the bill number on it, and enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope when you want a receipt.

sections.h2: What is Lowndes County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Lowndes is a south Georgia county of roughly 497 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau estimates 122,867 people lived there on July 1, 2025. That is 3.9% above the 2020 base of 118,259, a slower climb than the 8.0% logged in Lumpkin County or the 33.5% in Long County.

QuickFacts puts the density at 237.8 people per square mile in 2020 and counts 54,425 housing units. Owners live in 56.9% of occupied homes, and the middle value of an owner-occupied home is $215,600 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income is $58,541, and 18.1% of residents are in poverty. The average trip to work is only 19.5 minutes, the shortest among the four Georgia places in this set.

The Census lists 804 building permits for 2025. Retail sales in 2022 reached about $2.64 billion, and health care and social assistance receipts were about $1.07 billion that year.

sections.h2: When are Lowndes County property taxes due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property tax is generally due by November 15 each year. The commissioner mails bills at least 60 days before that date, and the county's tax information page says bills go out during the first week of October.

Lowndes County property tax calendar and late charges, as the tax commissioner publishes them
ItemWhat the commissioner's site says
Property returnsFiled January 1 through April 1
Homestead applicationReceived by April 1 to count that year
Appeal of assessmentWithin 45 days of the assessment notice
Due date, real estateGenerally November 15; weekend or holiday moves to next business day
Interest after due dateBank prime rate plus 3%, added monthly
Penalty5% of tax due at 120 days after the due date, repeated every 120 days, capped at 20%
Penalty exceptionHomesteaded property with a bill under $500.00
Lien (FiFa)Recorded if unpaid, listed on the General Execution Docket

Source: Lowndes County Tax Commissioner FAQ and tax bill information pages.

Mailed payments need a postmark on or before the due date. The commissioner also lets owners pay in two installments, though interest and penalty apply to whatever stays unpaid after the due date. Because the date can change, the page tells owners to read the due date on the bill itself.

sections.h2: How do assessments and appeals work in Lowndes County?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes 40% of fair market value, and the Lowndes assessors set that value each year. Owners may file a return between January 1 and April 1 to declare a proposed value. If the Board of Assessors disagrees, it mails an assessment notice with its own number, and the county's tax information page says those notices go out in May.

To dispute the number, you have 45 days from the date on the notice. The appeal goes to the Lowndes County Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. After a decision, you can carry the matter to Superior Court by mailing or filing a written notice with the Board of Tax Assessors.

  • Value disputes start with the assessors at (229) 671-2540.
  • Billing disputes start with the commissioner at 229-671-2579.
  • One mill is one dollar of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, and the commissioners and the Board of Education each set a rate every year.

After value is settled, the commissioner subtracts exemptions from the assessed value and multiplies the remainder by the millage rate. For the actual Lowndes rate, read your current bill, since the rate changes each year.

sections.h2: What payment options does the Lowndes County commissioner list?
sections.html:
Owners can pay in person, by mail, in the drive-up box, or by credit card. The office states that a card payment carries a convenience fee charged by the card company: 2.57% for Discover, Mastercard and Visa, and 3% for American Express, with a $1.50 minimum on each.

The office does not mail delinquent bills monthly, only at certain intervals, so verify the amount due before sending a payment. Interest keeps adding every month until the balance is paid, and the lien stays on a credit record for a minimum of seven years according to the commissioner's page.

If taxes stay unpaid more than 90 days after they are due, the county's tax information page says the Delinquent Tax Office may begin tax sale proceedings. Ask the commissioner before then about the exact balance and steps.

sections.h2: What happens if you sell a Lowndes County house with tax still unpaid?
sections.html:
The bill goes to the owner of record on January 1, and a lien is recorded in that January 1 owner's name unless the commissioner receives a contract or closing statement within 90 days of the due date showing the new owner took responsibility. Sellers who prorated the tax at closing should carry a copy of that statement to the Patterson Street office.

The state rule is plain: if you owned the property on January 1, you owe that year's ad valorem tax for the whole year, with no refund for a sale on January 2. A buyer can still be billed too, since the commissioner mails a bill to the new owner when the deed transfer reaches the office.

If you receive a bill for a house you already sold, forward it to the new owner. Selling an inherited or tenant-occupied house in Lowndes County follows the same path: get a payoff from the commissioner, then let the closing attorney handle the payoff at the table.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special programs reduce Lowndes County tax?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the common one for residences, and the freeport exemption is the common one for business personal property. You must own and occupy the home on January 1, and you apply at the Tax Assessor's Office.

  • Apply any time during the year, but the office must receive the application by April 1 for it to apply that year; later ones roll to the next year.
  • Once granted, the exemption continues in the same house. If you move, you apply again for the new address.
  • At age 65, an owner can apply for an additional homestead exemption, according to the commissioner's FAQ.
  • Special assessment programs, such as farm and conservation use, are explained by the assessors.

Mobile and modular homes are personal property, and the commissioner's FAQ says the owner of any one located in the county must file a return.

faqs.q: When is Lowndes County property tax due?
faqs.a: Generally by November 15 each year for real estate and business personal property. Read the due date on your own bill, because the commissioner says it can change.

faqs.q: What penalty does Lowndes County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Interest runs at the bank prime rate plus 3% each month, and a 5% penalty applies 120 days after the due date, repeating every 120 days up to 20%. Homesteaded property with a bill under $500.00 is exempt from the penalty.

faqs.q: Can I pay Lowndes County property tax in two payments?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner's office allows two payments, though interest and penalty apply to any balance left unpaid after the due date.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my Lowndes County deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Superior Court, on the first floor of the Lowndes County Judicial Complex at 327 N. Ashley Street in Valdosta, supplies copies of your warranty deed.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Lowndes County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. Appeal to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and then you may continue to Superior Court by written notice to the assessors.
